headline_marked: [[New pay scale gazette delayed]] 15 days after cabinet approval; govt employees await notification
headline: New pay scale gazette delayed 15 days after cabinet approval; govt employees await notification
summary: Despite cabinet approval 15 days ago, the gazette notification for the new pay scale for government employees is yet to be issued. The delay is due to ongoing vetting processes before it goes to the Law Ministry.
details: Government employees are still awaiting the gazette notification for the new pay scale, 15 days after it received cabinet approval. The delay has left many wondering about the reasons behind the hold-up.

Sources indicate that various aspects of the new pay scale are currently under scrutiny. Once these processes are complete, the proposal will be sent to the Law Ministry for vetting, after which the Finance Ministry will issue the gazette.

Dr. Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, the Prime Minister's Finance and Planning Advisor, stated that every step of the pay scale implementation is being properly completed. He affirmed there is no room to question whether it will be implemented.

The last national pay scale for government employees was announced in 2015, with the gazette notification issued approximately three and a half months after cabinet approval. This time, there was an expectation of a quicker gazette after the August 31 approval.

The Finance Division is actively working on drafting the gazette. It is anticipated that five separate special orders (SROs) will be issued for different categories and institutions of government employees.

While the cabinet approved the salary and allowance increases for various grades, detailed instructions are now being prepared on how the new pay scale will be implemented for each officer and employee.

Separate directives will also be issued for the pay, allowances, and other benefits of personnel in the defense forces, BGB, police, government financial institutions, and autonomous bodies. A high-level secretary committee is overseeing this coordination.

The new pay scale maintains 20 grades, setting the minimum salary at BDT 20,000 and the maximum at BDT 156,000, effective from July 1. Former Secretary Abdul Awal Majumder emphasized the importance of carefully reviewing the language and legal terminology in the draft gazette.

headline_marked: [[ICT-2 to deliver verdict today]] in crimes against humanity case against Obaidul Quader, 6 others
headline: ICT-2 to deliver verdict today in crimes against humanity case against Obaidul Quader, 6 others
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 will announce its decision in the case involving atrocities during the 2024 quota reform movement, following an eight-month trial. All seven accused, including Obaidul Quader, are currently absconding.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case. The case involves Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others, accused of atrocities committed during the July uprising in 2024.
After approximately eight months of trial, the tribunal announced yesterday that the verdict would be delivered today. All seven individuals accused in the case are currently absconding.

The accused include Obaidul Quader, former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, its General Secretary Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and its General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

The prosecution alleges that Quader, as AL general secretary and a cabinet minister, exercised command and control over law enforcement agencies and armed cadres. This was purportedly to violently suppress the quota reform movement, which began on July 1, 2024.

It is further alleged that over 1,400 protesters were killed and more than 25,000 seriously injured. These casualties reportedly resulted from widespread, systematic, and targeted attacks on the civilian population, carried out with the knowledge and involvement of the accused.
Nasim is accused of helping organise and facilitate the party’s response, while Arafat allegedly played a role in controlling media and suppressing reports of killings and violence.

Parash and Nikhil were accused of mobilising Jubo League activists, with the prosecution alleging Nikhil himself opened fire on protesters. BCL leaders Saddam and Enan were accused of assembling armed cadres and coordinating attacks.

The investigation began on June 18, 2025, and the trial commenced on February 17, with 29 prosecution witnesses testifying. Both prosecution and defence completed their closing arguments from August 4 to 17.
caption:
